headline: Conspiracy Update: Government Surveillance Pigeons 'Went Rogue in 2024,' Now Freelance
subheadline: Former believers in bird-drone theory pivot to explain increasingly chaotic pigeon behavior
summary: The 'Birds Aren't Real' movement has updated its lore to explain why pigeons seem less organized than proper surveillance would require.
content:
The "Birds Aren't Real" movement has issued a major lore update: government surveillance pigeons, they claim, "went rogue" in early 2024 and are now operating as freelance agents.

The revision addresses a long-standing criticism of the bird-drone theory: if pigeons are surveillance devices, why do they behave so chaotically? Why do they walk into traffic? Why do they fight each other over bread?

"The contract ended," explains movement spokesperson @BirdWatcher_Truth. "January 2024, the pigeons' government contract wasn't renewed. Budget cuts. So now they're freelancing. Selling data to whoever pays—corporations, foreign governments, that guy who feeds them in the park."

The theory suggests this explains recent changes in pigeon behavior. "Notice how they've gotten bolder?" @BirdWatcher_Truth continued. "That's because they're not following protocol anymore. They're entrepreneurs now. Hustle culture."

The update has been controversial within the bird-drone community. Traditionalists argue that birds remain fully government-controlled, while reformists embrace the freelance narrative.

"The pigeons in my city have been acting different since 2024," reported one convert. "More aggressive. More... entrepreneurial. One made direct eye contact with me for 47 seconds. That's not surveillance. That's a sales pitch."

Ornithologists have declined to comment, with one noting they're "exhausted" by requests to debunk increasingly elaborate bird theories.

The movement has begun selling merchandise reading "Support Your Local Freelance Pigeon" with proceeds going to an undisclosed cause. When asked where the money goes, @BirdWatcher_Truth responded: "The pigeons need startup capital. We're helping them pivot."

At press time, a pigeon outside the reporter's window appeared to be taking notes.
author: Alex Rivera, Digital Culture
